cellularautomata.name: Cellular Automata: What a Neighbour Can Change
cellularautomata.truth: A field keeps states at addresses. Its neighbourhood, update schedule, boundary and input determine how those states can change.
cellularautomata.qfep_connection: The reflective track asks who or what can contribute, what a stored state retains, and how a receiver turns a value into a consequence. These are situated questions; this sequence does not measure Langton’s lambda or demonstrate a universal edge-of-chaos condition.
cellularautomata.demonstration: Step a row, follow a fading cell, walk beside a saved history, connect Life to a lamp, withdraw support by proximity, isolate exchange and measure one changed beginning.
cellularautomata.description: Eight museum comparisons: local answers, lingering states, retained history, moving patterns, bodily input, neighbour exchange, different procedures and matched differences.
cellularautomata.estimated_time: Self-paced; no measured completion time for the eight build-and-investigate lessons.
learning_objectives: Read ordered Boolean neighbours and update from an unchanged previous row.
Separate cell state, active participation and visible surface in a three-state volume.
Keep independent history and distinguish site, generation, display and physical support.
Implement Life and connect a fixed address to an output without feedback.
Transform external positions into rule inputs; compare synchronous and scan updates.
Isolate neighbour exchange from a shared local reaction using matched fields.
Distinguish local state updates from a supplied recursive placement recipe.
Measure matched differences and separate storage, threshold and display gain.

artifact_groups.rationale: A held row, a mirrored rug, and twenty recorded stages of a line network distinguish local rules, imposed symmetry and the history a drawing keeps.
Recrystallization and self-organization; building blocks of CA growth patterns
CA showcase: columns, mirrored automata, bridge structures, and natural phenomena
Beyond binary: hexagonal CA, growth networks, petri dish life, and mold network dynamics
Expanding into space: 3D tree growth, crossway patterns, decay, and fractal chair exploration
Soft rules: stochastic Rule 30/110 gravity and CA on spherical non-planar topology
Agents and circuits: interactive rule explorer, 3D stacked automata, and Sierpinski fractal
Edge of chaos: screen display, self-organization, disease spread, and volumetric fog CA
